title: Protocol for conducting bibliometric analysis in biomedicine using CiteSpace and VOSviewer
author: Du, Zhao, et al.
materials: At present, researchers commonly utilize the Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, PubMed or Google Scholar database for data collection and CiteSpace and VOSviewer software for visualizing knowledge maps. This methodology relies on the capabilities of these tools.1.Verify that the affiliated institution possesses access to the WoS, Scopus, PubMed or Google Scholar database, particularly the WoS Core Collection.2.Acquire and install an authorized version of CiteSpace.3.Install VOSviewer software to complement the analysis and visualization capabilities provided by CiteSpace.Note: Utilize unlicensed software can result in the loss of crucial node data, which may render the visualization analysis unreliable and unpredictable.

steps.title: Verify access and install software
steps.instruction: Confirm that the institution has access to the Web of Science Core Collection (or Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar). Acquire an authorized copy of CiteSpace and install it. Download VOSviewer from www.vosviewer.com/download and install the latest version. Note: using unlicensed software may cause loss of node data and unreliable visualizations.

substeps.instruction: Check institutional subscriptions to WoS Core Collection (or alternative databases).
Obtain a licensed CiteSpace package and run its installer.
Visit the VOSviewer website, download the current version, and follow the installation prompts.

steps.title: Extract and clean WoS data
steps.instruction: Use Web of Science to retrieve the full set of records for the chosen topic, explore publication attributes, extract required fields, and export the data in plain‑text format while respecting the 500‑record export limit.

substeps.instruction: Search WoS with the desired query (e.g., mitochondrial therapies).
Explore each record’s attributes: publication year, authors, institutions, countries/regions, journal, Journal Citation Reports data, and keywords.
Use the “Analyze Results” function to view aggregated data such as publication years, authors, titles, and countries/regions.
Export all records in “Plain Text” format; because WoS only supports 500 records per export, perform multiple exports if needed.
Name each exported file using the pattern “download_xxx-xxx”.

steps.title: Record basic publication characteristics
steps.instruction: From the WoS export, generate tables of the top‑10 entities for countries/regions, institutions, authors, and journals, including number of publications, total citations, and average citations.

substeps.instruction: Create Table 4 – Institutions: Sun Yat‑Sen University 274 (362 5 13.23), Shanghai Jiao Tong University 267 (338 6 12.68), Chinese Academy of Sciences 255 (412 8 16.19), Fudan University 249 (337 7 13.56), Zhejiang University 228 (309 8 13.59), Nanjing Medical University 198 (207 4 10.47), Southern Medical University 188 (179 9 5.55), Sichuan University 180 (230 8 12.82), Central South University 172 (190 3 11.06), Huazhong University of Science and Technology 167 (265 0 15.87).

Create Table 6 – Journals: International Journal of Molecular Sciences 399 (257 36 45), Cancers 182 (142 27 84), Scientific Reports 178 (146 78 24), Cell Death & Disease 165 (240 8 14.59), Free Radical Biology and Medicine 140 (217 5 15.54), Nature Communications 139 (388 5 27.95), Redox Biology 138 (311 4 22.57), Frontiers In Pharmacology 132 (144 5 10.95), Antioxidants 120 (79 5 6.63), Cells 116 (78 7 6.78).

steps.title: Install and set up VOSviewer
steps.instruction: Download the latest VOSviewer version, install it, and verify that the exported WoS file is a plain‑text file compatible with VOSviewer.

substeps.instruction: Go to www.vosviewer.com/download and download the current installer.
Run the installer and follow on‑screen instructions.
Confirm that the WoS export is a plain‑text (.txt) file.

steps.title: Create VOSviewer maps
steps.instruction: Import the plain‑text file into VOSviewer, choose the appropriate map type, adjust visualization settings, generate the map, explore clusters, and export the final figures.

substeps.instruction: Open VOSviewer and select “Create a map based on text data” for keyword maps or “Create a map based on bibliographic data” for citation maps.
Upload the plain‑text file and follow the prompts.
Adjust settings (e.g., clustering resolution, label size) as needed.
Click “Create” to generate the visualization (maps for countries/regions, institutions, journals, etc.).
Use interactive tools to zoom, explore connections, and interpret patterns.
Export the completed visualizations in the desired image format (Figures 5‑7).

steps.title: Install and configure CiteSpace
steps.instruction: Download CiteSpace Basic, install the required Java runtime, create the necessary folder structure, and convert the WoS exports into CiteSpace‑readable format.

substeps.instruction: Visit https://citespace.podia.com/download and download the Basic version.
Install CiteSpace and ensure a compatible Java runtime environment is configured.
Create three folders in the working directory named “data”, “project”, and “input”.
Copy all WoS plain‑text files into the “input” folder.
In CiteSpace, read the files from “input”, convert them to the internal format, and export the results to the “data” folder.

steps.title: Run CiteSpace keyword analysis
steps.instruction: Perform keyword co‑occurrence analysis, adjust the network layout, conduct clustering, and export the results.

substeps.instruction: Open CiteSpace, ensure the “data” folder is loaded.
Set the time slice to 1 year; keep all other parameters at default except those in the Node Types module.
Select the “Keywords” module and run the analysis.
If the network appears crowded, use the Pruning option and adjust node distances.
Drag nodes to improve visual dispersion.
Run cluster analysis, then export the clustering results.
Integrate the cluster labels into the visualization (Figure 8).

steps.title: Run CiteSpace authorship analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct author‑keyword co‑occurrence analysis, refine the visualization, cluster, and export the outcomes.

substeps.instruction: Select both the “Author” and “Keywords” modules.
Run the co‑occurrence analysis.
Drag nodes to fine‑tune the layout.
Perform cluster analysis and export the results.
Add the clustering labels to the map (Figure 9).

steps.title: Analyze highly cited publications
steps.instruction: Identify the top‑10 % most cited papers (2020‑2024), extract key bibliographic data, and visualize them using the same VOSviewer/CiteSpace workflows.

substeps.instruction: In WoS, filter for publications in the top 10 % of citations within the 2020‑2024 window.
Read each abstract individually and record author(s), year, and other relevant information.
Export these records in plain‑text format (respecting the 500‑record limit).
Apply the VOSviewer and CiteSpace procedures described earlier to generate visualizations for the highly cited set (Figure 10).

steps.title: Check for duplicate entries
steps.instruction: Review the generated visualizations for redundant institutional names and keywords, and remove or merge duplicates to improve clarity.
